course.title: Supply Chain Analytics
course.description: This course provides students with a comprehensive foundation in simulating business processes to analyze performance, improve efficiency, and support decision-making. Students will explore the principles of discrete-event simulation, system variability, and process flow logic through hands-on experience with industry-standard tools Arena. The course covers the full simulation lifecycle, including process mapping, data input collection, model building, experimentation, and result interpretation. Emphasis is placed on identifying operational bottlenecks, testing what-if scenarios, and developing optimization strategies. By the end of the course, students will be able to construct realistic simulation models and use them to evaluate and improve real-world systems in manufacturing, logistics, and service operations.

clos.description: CLO 1: To explain fundamental concepts of simulation in the context of real-world business and supply chain operation. - LLO 1.1: To explain components of Module entities including create, process, dispose, decide, record. - LLO 1.2: To explain components of Spreadsheet entities including entities, resource, queue, variable, attribute, and statistics. - LLO 1.3: To explain others components including waiting time, number of waiting, resource utilization, capacity, and run set up.

CLO 2: To study features of ARENA software by solving simple problems in business and supply chain context. - LLO 2.1: To explore features of ARENA and use it to solve problems. - LLO 2.2: To modify model based on instruction and visualize through graph. - LLO 2.3: To create different scenarios for cross- case comparison and propose a practical solution based on real world context
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Lab 1 Report Lab 2 Report Lab 3 Report Midterm Exam

clos.description: CLO 3: To construct simulation model in ARENA Software to solve complex problems in business and supply chain context. - LLO 3.1: To define type of distribution using Input Analyzer tool to input data in ARENA. - LLO 3.2: To fasten optimization process by using Process Analyzer tool. - LLO 3.3: To define possible solutions and select the best one using Opt-Quest Tool.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Lab 4 Report Lab 5 Report Lab 6 Report Final Exam

clos.description: CLO 4: To solve a real-world project using ARENA and communicate finding with stakeholders based on local business context. - LLO 4.1: To build a power point to share research finding and its practical solution to class - LLO 4.2: To present research finding by convincing and sell solutions to the stakeholders. - LLO 4.3: To draft research article using format provided
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Proposal presentation Final report Final presentation

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Students are responsible for understanding how to use resources responsibly. Not knowing the rules, misunderstanding the rules, running out of time, submitting “the wrong draft,” or being overwhelmed with multiple demands are not acceptable excuses. There are no excuses for failure to uphold academic integrity. Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Form a study group and take full advantage of such an opportunity to share the understanding with classmates. Thoughtful participation in class discussions, thorough preparations for the class, and consistently well-developed responses to the assignments are expected. Students are expected to explain lessons to each other and have self-study from the other source. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned Submit assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Course policy Policy for Description Attendance Students Must attend class on-site and on-time (Three lates is counted as a one-time absence). Must do self-study and read the relevant documents in the Internet/library. Academic Integrity & Collaboration Students Must complete assigned tasks (assignments, quizzes, and exams) only by himself/herself. Questions might be asked during/after submission Must join class activities actively Must work independently on the midterm and final exam. Should discuss course material with other students Must feel guilty if they: (1) present work of others as their own, and (2) give unauthorized assistance to other students. Homework Students Must complete and submit assignment tasks on time. Must proper justifying quotations from appropriate and authorized resources. Must use APA style for in-text citation and reference list. Penalties Students Can absent (Absent + Permission) at most 5 times per course; otherwise, they will need to repeat the same course in the following year. Get one absent if they get three late (Students are considered as late, when they join class after 5 min start) Will be accused of plagiarism, if they (1) present work of others as their own, and (2) give unauthorized assistance to other, and get scored Zero. Will be deducted score if they submit classwork or homework late Will be reported to the Study Office, and handled in accordance with the university regulations if they violate the university code of conducts Note: If you are unclear whether a particular situation may violate the university code of conducts, you should ask the instructor.
